II23A-01.note: Cadfield (heat only) vs Aldmoss (heat+dredge) isolates dredging. A (Dellow>Aldmoss) is the tempting confounded comparison; D reverses the clean SE/SW contrast; C supports Faulk.

II23A-02.note: Logged-no-worm Corlett lighter than worm-only Ambersley says logging outweighs worms. A is the tempting clean worm contrast but supports; C weakens Elling; B is the slope confound.

II23A-03.note: Same-garden comparison of city vs rural ordinary seeds. A (different gardens) is the tempting confound; D carries the heavy-seed confound; B is a reversal and easy to strike.

II23A-04.note: Same pre-2010 year, burned-only Daleford beats fenced Carbery. C mixes a wet year with a dry one; D supports Cole without touching fences; B supports fences.

II23A-05.note: Bramel (7 mites, no orchard) storing less than Ardane (3, orchard) supports mites despite pesticide working against it. C is the reversed Elvey/Ardane contrast; D is the upland confound; B supports Dacosta.

II23A-06.note: Benvoray: 6.2 rats/ha and 0.65 chicks/nest. Ardvane has the best ratio but only 4 rats/ha; Caillin and Dunvarra pass the rat bar but fall below 0.6.

II23A-07.note: Limit is 1.5 m above the bolt, so Cendry (1.3) is below it; D is the strong trap for students who ignore the 0.4 m offset. A and C compare the wrong direction or two sites above the limit.

II23A-08.note: Copperhill drops 8 points and ripens in 66 days. Birchtop is tempting (fast, but drops 13); Emberglow and Dawnlight pass the drop but ripen later than Amberlee's 71.

II23B-01.note: Leaky-far Ingold beats plastic-near-quarry Harrowfield on matched thick soil. A reverses the clean Ingold/Jorvenn pair; B and C carry the thin-soil confound.

II23B-02.note: Meltwater-only Hamrin later than cliff-only Isel. B tests cliffs; C confounds both factors; D is the reverse direction.

II23B-03.note: Injection-only Gisler after 2012 beats fracking-only Kvamby after 2014. A (Hollis has both) is the tempting confound; D has the fault-zone confound; C runs the wrong way.

II23B-04.note: Kvist (300 hikers) losing less than Gorrel (120), both horse-free and gentle. B weakens Hennum instead; D has the steep-slope confound; A supports.

II23B-05.note: Possibly defective: I find no option that cleanly weakens Hagelin. C (Gullhaven 2018 > Kelstad 2018, before irrigation) supports her, A and D carry the Ljorn clay confound, and B is a cross-year comparison that irrigation explains. Picked B only by elimination.

II23B-06.note: Ivesk: 95 m, 2.25 L/s/m. Grinde exceeds 2 but is only 60 m deep; Hallum (1.94) is a near-miss; Jaren is 1.67.

II23B-07.note: Iskilde fell 41 to 30, then rose 26.7%. Ludal fell but rose only 15%; Granberg rose more than 20% but never fell. Hjelset is easy to strike.

II23B-08.note: Jassel (beyond, 3.4) vs Gyllen (inside, 1.6) gives 2.1x. C is the trap (Kolbeck/Hennick, only 1.8x); B puts Ivra beyond the line by its far point; A compares two inside asteroids.

II23C-01.note: On the flat plain, stations-only Nettleford beats lanes-only Mossgate. B has the slope confound and is tempting; D weakens Ruddock instead.

II23C-02.note: Both are rail towns without bus lanes; only Mellick charges on weekdays. A is the rail/bus confound; B reverses; C is the rail confound.

II23C-03.note: Neither Nethercote nor Quellin has cul-de-sacs; only one has porches. B (Morwen > Quellin) is the tempting confound; A and D weaken.

II23C-04.note: Ruskett (neither, near market) beats Merrigal (extension, near). C has the distance confound; A supports; D concerns credit.

II23C-05.note: In 2017, tax-only Quorley vs untreated Mistlow. D is the tempting within-town drop, but the background decline and the 2016 campaign confound it; A supports Quarrie; C reverses.

II23C-06.note: The line is at 4 km, so Moxley (6) is past it and outsells Rindell (1). B puts Padstone (inside) over Oberwick; D reverses; C compares two inside stations.

II23C-07.note: Mavisford: 3.7 books per resident at 52 km. Ollerby clears the bar but is 18 km; Pembray is a 2.94 near-miss; Quintard is 2.6.

II23C-08.note: Quillow: 81.8% finished, +$4.20. Prestley finished 83% but gained only $3.90; Nanbury gained $4.50 but finished 65%. The options state only the after-wage, so before-wages must come from the table.

II23D-01.note: Sellwick's sales fell after the 1840 railway. A supports; B and D carry the market confound.

II23D-02.note: Both upland; schooled off-road Stavely beats unschooled on-road Tessaby. A (40 vs 15 years) is the tempting option but Vintrell is also on the road; B is the valley effect; D crosses regions.

II23D-03.note: Both on the headland; company-only Sallowby beats ordinance-only Vexley. D is the tempting harbor/headland confound; B and C weaken.

II23D-04.note: In the same year, mills-only Tenlow beats board-only Sudmere. A crosses the 1858 slump; C weakens Vasquez; B supports.

II23D-05.note: Within Sarnby the conservatory treats both groups the same, so clerks over shopkeepers isolates installment plans. A is the tempting cross-town confound; C is about the conservatory.

II23D-06.note: Stennard 2.19x with 320 seats. Tavisholm more than doubled but has 610 seats; Ulvercote (1.87x) is the near-miss. The options give only the 1900 figure, which is weaker than real SAT phrasing because the option alone does not show the claim.

II23D-07.note: Tarnside: 18.6 visitors per painting, 27.6% sold. Yoxholt passes the visitor bar but sold 23.8%; Uxley sold 26% but drew 23 per painting.

II23D-08.note: Vardleigh: 8 outlets, 1,175 residents each. Wickerby is a 1,320 near-miss with the largest counts; Sedgeholm passes but has a grammar school.
